requirement: The outline uses the file snapshot retained by the domain’s cache. Each item includes its kind and a reference the agent can pass to `read_node`. Follow `next` to see more items.
rationale:
The requirement has three obligations. Each has a test with assertions that enforce it.

1. **Snapshot retention.** `src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_continuations_keep_the_file_and_complete_ordered_items]` outlines `code.rs` and then overwrites the file on disk with `fn changed() {}`. It outlines the same node again and asserts that `items` equals the first outline. A live re-read would give one item instead of 401, so the test would catch it. The other tests also exercise the outline paths without domain reads:
   - `outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads` asserts there are no domain reads.
   - `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` asserts there are no dependencies.
   - `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[cached_selected_source_reads_record_exact_delivered_contents_and_errors_add_no_input]` outlines a cached provider source whose text differs from the current source.

2. **Kind and read_node reference on each item.**
   - The continuation test checks every item for `node` (the interned `code.rs#fn[item_N]`), `file`, `selector` and `kind` (`fn`, or empty for the root). It then passes an item (`items[5]`) to `read_node` and checks that the text comes back.
   - `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_outlines_present_every_top_level_and_nested_item]` asserts the exact ordered nodes with `selector` and `kind`, including the nested `impl[Thing]/fn[nested]`.
   - `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_tools_forward_arguments_and_present_discovery_and_read_results]` checks that the outline carries the resource and the kind for `fn[chosen]`.
   - `outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads` checks that items have numeric `node` references.

3. **Following `next`.** The continuation test builds 400 items, so the outline spans more than one page. It follows `next` through `get_next_page` until the last page. For each page it checks that the page is non-empty and keeps the same `node`, and it checks that no dependencies are recorded. Across pages it checks that the item count and order are complete (401 items, in order). It also checks that invalid and unknown UUIDs are rejected.

All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no untested obligations.
